old.title: Bone Mass Measurement (DXA) (Synthetic)
verification_notes: Synthetic fictional policy generated from a scenario specification; not CMS guidance.

sections.heading: Coverage Indications
sections.text:
This section describes the indications for which bone mass measurement may be covered.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with a history of fragility fracture.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for estrogen-deficient women at clinical risk for osteoporosis.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with primary hyperparathyroidism.
- Bone mass measurement is considered reasonable and necessary for beneficiaries with vertebral abnormalities on imaging.

sections.heading: Eligibility Criteria
sections.text:
Coverage requires that all of the following criteria are met:
The results will be used to guide treatment decisions. The beneficiary has a documented diagnosis of osteoporosis. The treating practitioner expects measurable improvement within a predictable period. The beneficiary is at least 50 years of age.

sections.heading: Limitations and Exclusions
sections.text:
The following limitations apply:
- Peripheral bone density testing used only for screening is not covered.
- Testing more often than the frequency limit is not covered without documented medical necessity.

sections.heading: Frequency and Duration
sections.text: Bone mass measurement is limited to 1 scan every 24 months.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence Required for Coverage
sections.text:
The following clinical evidence is required:
Results of dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry obtained within 18 months before the initial scan must be available.

sections.heading: Documentation Requirements for the Medical Record
sections.text:
The following documentation must be available upon request:
1. Documentation must state the clinical reason any scan was missed or discontinued.
2. The treating practitioner must document a face-to-face evaluation within 30 days before the initial scan.
3. The medical record must contain a signed and dated order for bone mass measurement from the treating practitioner.
4. A plan of care that specifies goals, frequency and expected duration must be on file before bone mass measurement begins.

sections.heading: Practitioner Qualifications and Supervision
sections.text:
The following qualifications apply:
1. Facilities furnishing bone mass measurement must maintain written protocols for emergency response.
2. Staff furnishing bone mass measurement must hold current basic life support certification.
3. Bone mass measurement must be furnished under personal supervision of a physician.

sections.heading: Covered Diagnosis Codes (ICD-10-CM)
sections.text:
Claims must include one of the following ICD-10-CM codes:
- E21.3 - Hyperparathyroidism, unspecified
- E28.310 - Symptomatic premature menopause
- Z79.52 - Long term (current) use of systemic steroids

sections.heading: Billing and Coding Guidelines
sections.text:
The following billing instructions apply:
Services that do not meet the criteria in this policy should be reported with the modifier indicating that denial is expected. Services must be billed with the place of service code that reflects where the scan was furnished.

sections.heading: Summary of Evidence and Rationale
sections.text: Published studies report improvements in fracture risk assessment among beneficiaries receiving bone mass measurement. Studies with longer follow-up show that benefits decline without continued adherence.

sections.heading: Implementation
sections.text: The requirements of this policy apply to services performed on or after 02/01/2020.

sections.heading: Sources of Information
sections.text:
- Fictional Society of Radiology. Clinical practice guideline for osteoporosis. 2014 edition.
- Synthetic Evidence Review Group. Systematic review of bone mass measurement outcomes. 2021.

findings.recommended_action: Obtain and compare the replacement policy before the retirement date, and update references in workflows and claim edits.
